newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia Airline System Bhd results.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Malaysia Airline System Bhd results.

text.p: Following are reactions to the full-year results to March 31, 1997 announced by Malaysian Airline System Bhd, showing a leap in net profit to 332.86 million rinngit from 232.94 million the previous year.
SHAMSUL SHAMSUDIN, AVIATION ANALYST AT PESAKA JARDINE FLEMING

"It's in line with my forecast and about 14 percent above market expectations in the Estimates Directory. I was expecting around 280 million (ringgit) and the market 252.2 million. So leaving out the aircraft sales of around 44 million, it tallies.
"From the very basic numbers, it appears that they have benefitted from a long-term, fuel-cost arrangement with Petronas."
CHOO SWEE KEE, INVESTMENT ANALYST AT VICKERS BALLAS:
"We were looking at around 270 (million ringgit) and its slightly above our expectations.
"One look at it, you can tell that they've benefited from the lower tax rate on the net side. (Operating) margin wise, there seems to be a slight improvement also.
SEBASTIAN CHANG, RESEARCH MANAGER AT MOHAIYANI SECURITIES:
"It's much higher than market expectations because jet fuel costs went up an average 19 percent year-on-year in 1996.
"I think the full impact of their cost-cutting exercise has taken place. (MAS chairman) Tan Sri Tajudin (Ramli) has been on a cost-cutting exercise since he took over the airline."
